prerequisites: Basic knowledge of electrical engineering such as network calculation methods and the fundamentals of electromagnetic fields.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have expanded their knowledge of electrical engineering fundamentals to include three-phase systems and transformers.
Students will know the basic structure and function of electrical power systems and their components.

Students will have learned about basic components of electrical power supply, such as the most important power plant generators, lines, power plant types, and grid types, and can reproduce their function or analytical description.
Students will have learned to apply and combine the knowledge acquired in the fundamentals of electrical engineering to specific questions of electrical power engineering.

Students will know typical questions from electrical power engineering and have derived the methodology for their development from the fundamentals of electrical engineering and can apply these methods.

Students can evaluate the specific properties of individual power engineering components (e.g., generator, line, transformer, power electronic converter) with regard to their significance for the system context.
Students are able to abstract from detail to the essential to analyze the interaction of different system components in electrical power engineering.

Students are able to critically reflect on current issues of electrical power supply arising against the backdrop of the ongoing energy transition and the overall societal sustainability discussions, and to evaluate them on a scientific basis.
Students can derive approaches for resource-efficient, economically sensible, and supply-secure handling of electrical energy from the learned technological contexts.
Students can critically reflect on new approaches to handling electrical energy, having learned the scientific basic relationships.
Students can prepare results of selected analyses and calculations, present them in a group, discuss them with experts, and explain them.

syllabus_topics: Energy transmission - Transformers, lines and grids
Practical with experiments on the generation, distribution and application of electrical energy.
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a 120-minute written exam. The ungraded assessment is experimental work consisting of a total of five experiments. Both components must be successfully completed to be awarded ECTS credits.
